description: The bar N bars ago engulfs the bar before it, reaching at or beyond both extremes and strictly beyond at least one, with an optional tick tolerance for an almost-outside bar.
pseudocode: high[lag] >= high[lag+1] - toleranceTicks * tickSize && low[lag] <= low[lag+1] + toleranceTicks * tickSize && (high[lag] > high[lag+1] || low[lag] < low[lag+1])

complexity.reason: two-bar comparison plus a tick offset

catalog_match.note: No outside-bar rule in the catalog.

merge_notes: R00-04 and V00-05 make both sides inclusive, which lets an identical-range bar be inside AND outside at once; T00-05 and T07-01 require strictly beyond on one side, and that reading won. V16-06's near-outside bar is toleranceTicks 1. V09-04 is the same test at lag 1, placed negated to block breakout entries off an outside bar. Absorbed the directional variants: T07-34 (outside bull bar completing a two-bar reversal), R00-06 (outside DOWN bar) and T21-68 (outside UP bar) are OutsideBar ANDed with the bar body direction, which the pane system supplies per placement, so they are not separate rules.

description: The bar failed to extend the move: its high is at or below the prior bar's high plus a small tick tolerance (mirrored for the short side).

complexity.reason: one comparison plus a tick offset

catalog_match.note: At pauseTicks 0 this is exactly LaggedHigherHigh(lookback 0) placed negated. The tick tolerance is Brooks's 'or only a tick or so higher', which is what makes it a separate rule; at the default 1 it fires on bars LaggedHigherHigh negated does not.

merge_notes: Only clean statement of the no-new-extreme pause in the bucket. Brooks scopes it to a bull trend and to small bars after a strong trend bar; both of those are separate filters and are left to the pane.

description: Quality marker of a strong bull reversal bar: it opens at or below the prior bar's close (no gap against the reversal) and closes above both its own open and the prior bar's close.
pseudocode: open[0] <= close[1] + nearTicks * tickSize && close[0] > open[0] && close[0] > close[1]

complexity.reason: two-bar arithmetic plus a tick offset

merge_notes: One rule from the same book sentence in two volumes. The threshold differs only in how 'near' is read: V00-31 and T00-40 use 1 tick, T05-02 reads 'near' as at-or-below and uses 0. Default 1, since 0 makes the tolerance input pointless; nearTicks = 0 recovers T05-02 exactly. tickSize is MinMove/PriceScale.

description: The bar has (near) zero tail above its body: the high is within N ticks of the higher of open and close - a shaved top (mirror: shaved bottom).

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic against a tick tolerance

merge_notes: R00-12 is declared 'same' sides but its own note says the shaved-bottom test is the mirror, so it is recorded here as mirrored - the per-placement side handling gets both. Body-based, unlike CloseNearBarExtreme which measures from the close; the two coincide only on bars whose close is the body extreme.

description: The bar has (near) zero tail at BOTH ends - open and close sit at or within N ticks of the high and the low.
pseudocode: (high[0] - max(open[0], close[0])) <= shaveTicks * tickSize && (min(open[0], close[0]) - low[0]) <= shaveTicks * tickSize
merge_notes: Not composable from ShavedBodyTop: that rule is mirrored, so a single placement can only ever test one end per side, and no combination of placements ANDs the top and bottom tests on the same side. Kept as its own direction-agnostic rule, which is also how the book states it ('no tail at either the top or the bottom').

description: The bar closes on, or within N ticks of, its own high (mirror: its own low) - urgency into the close.

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic against a tick tolerance

catalog_match.note: Same intent as a very high CloseRangePosition threshold, but this is an absolute tick tolerance, not a fraction of the bar's range - on a large bar the two disagree sharply.

merge_notes: Identical test in both volumes, both at 1 tick. T06-22 calls it a shaved bar; V00-46 calls it a spike bar closing on its high. Kept apart from ShavedBodyTop because that one measures from max(open, close), which differs from the close on every bear bar.

description: A two-bar reversal that occurs at a new N-bar extreme: the prior bar made a new N-bar low, and this bar closes up, above the prior close, while still overlapping the prior bar's low (mirror at a top).
pseudocode: low[1] <= lowest(low, swingLookback)[2] && close[0] > open[0] && close[0] > close[1] && low[0] <= low[1] + overlapTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: a lowest-low window plus two-bar arithmetic; no pivot detection needed

merge_notes: Kept apart from TwoBarReversal because the new-N-bar-extreme requirement is a behaviourally different rule, not a threshold: the plain two-bar reversal fires anywhere, this one only at a leg extreme. V01-07 states it from the bear side (a new high, close back below the two-bar midpoint) with lookback 10; V24-06 with 20. Default 20. Both replace Brooks's swing-pivot language with a plain lowest/highest window, which is the mechanizable reading.

description: The close clears the prior bar's high by an extra tick offset before the entry counts - a guard against one-tick traps (mirror below the prior low).

catalog_match.note: CloseAbovePriorHigh has only a bar-lookback input, no price offset, so the tick buffer cannot be reached from it. Not CloseNearPriorLow either - that compares against the opposite extreme in the opposite sense.

merge_notes: The offset is instrument-specific (Brooks says a couple of ticks for stocks, one tick generally), which is how CloseNearPriorLow's XX is already handled in the corpus. At offsetTicks = 0 this degenerates to the catalog rule.

description: Take a stop entry above the signal bar's high only if the entry bar OPENED below that stop level and then traded through it - skip the entry if the market gapped above the level (mirror for shorts).
pseudocode: open[0] < high[1] + entryTicks * tickSize && high[0] >= high[1] + entryTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: the current bar's open and high against the prior bar's high plus an offset

merge_notes: General entry hygiene, not specific to the wedge chapter it was mined from - it applies to every signal-bar breakout setup in the corpus. Distinct from PriorHighBreakoutWithOffset: this one adds a cap on the OPEN, which is the whole content of the rule.

description: The prior bar poked only a few ticks beyond the bar before it and this bar falls back through that level - a small failed breakout, common at the end of a protracted move and a signal in the opposite direction.
pseudocode: high[1] >= high[2] + failTicks * tickSize && low[0] < high[2] // short signal; mirror for the long

complexity.reason: three fixed-offset bars, once the reference extreme is taken as the bar before the poke rather than a remembered signal bar

merge_notes: Both sources state the same Emini-tuned five-or-nine-tick failed extension. V00-24 gives 5, R24-01 gives 9 with a 'near the end of a protracted trend' gate; that gate is dropped (it is the always-in/trend-duration decision, and V00-24 states the pattern without it), so this stays priority A rather than C. The fixed-offset reading of the reference extreme wins over 'the signal bar's high carried forward', per the mechanizability rule. failTicks is instrument-specific like CloseNearPriorLow's XX.

description: The bar's low comes within a few ticks of the N-bar lowest low without breaking it, and the bar closes up - the 'perfect test' that misses the clustered stops by a tick (mirror at a high).
pseudocode: priorLow = lowest(low, lookback)[1]; low[0] >= priorLow - marginTicks * tickSize && low[0] <= priorLow + marginTicks * tickSize && close[0] > open[0]

complexity.reason: a Lowest window plus a margin-band comparison

merge_notes: Deliberately the opposite of a failed breakout: the point is that price did NOT trade through the level. Kept separate from SmallTickFailedBreakoutReversal for that reason, and from StopRunReversalBar, which requires the break.
